name: Mojito
tagline: Mint, lime and rum over crushed ice.
intro: The Mojito is cool, bright and herbal, built right in the glass with muddled mint, lime and white rum. A splash of soda adds sparkle. It's one of the most refreshing drinks you can make on a warm day.
heroAlt: Engraved line illustration of a Mojito in a highball glass with mint and lime

glassware.name: Highball glass
glassware.note: A tall glass leaves room for plenty of ice and soda.

ingredients.note: A light, clean Cuban-style or Puerto Rican white rum works best.
Squeeze it fresh for the brightest flavor.
Superfine sugar dissolves most easily. Granulated is fine if you stir well.
Spearmint is the traditional choice for its sweet, cool flavor.
Chilled. Add a splash to finish, not to dilute.

steps.title: Wake up the mint
steps.body: Place the 8 mint leaves in your palm and give them a firm clap. This releases the aromatic oils without damaging the leaves.

steps.title: Muddle gently
steps.body: In the glass, add the mint, sugar and lime juice. Press the leaves lightly four or five times with the muddler.
steps.tip: Press, don't grind. Shredded mint turns bitter and leaves green flecks in the drink.

steps.title: Add the rum
steps.body: Pour in the 2 oz of white rum and stir for a few seconds until the sugar dissolves.

steps.title: Add crushed ice
steps.body: Fill the glass about two-thirds with crushed ice. If you don't have crushed ice, wrap cubes in a clean towel and smash them with a rolling pin.

steps.title: Churn
steps.body: Use a bar spoon to lift from the bottom and push up through the ice a few times. This mixes everything and chills the drink.

steps.title: Top with soda
steps.body: Pack more crushed ice on top, then add a splash of soda water to finish.

steps.title: Garnish
steps.body: Slap a fresh mint sprig lightly to release its aroma, then tuck it in alongside a lime wheel.
steps.tip: Place the straw close to the mint so you smell it as you sip.

tips: Pro tip: Use fresh, perky mint. Wilted mint tastes dull and grassy.
Pro tip: Dissolve the sugar in the lime juice before adding the ice. Sugar won't dissolve properly in cold liquid.
Common mistake: Over-muddling the mint, which makes the drink bitter.
Common mistake: Using too much soda. It should add lift, not wash out the rum and lime.

variations.name: Berry Mojito
variations.description: Muddle a few raspberries or blackberries with the mint and lime.

variations.name: Coconut Mojito
variations.description: Replace the white rum with coconut rum, or add a splash of coconut water.

variations.name: Virgin Mojito
variations.description: Leave out the rum and add extra soda water and a splash of lime.

variations.name: Dark Rum Mojito
variations.description: Use an aged rum for deeper vanilla and caramel flavors.

substitutions: Sugar: 2 tsp of simple syrup (about ½ oz) works if you don't have superfine sugar.
Mint: Spearmint is best. Peppermint is stronger and can taste medicinal.
Crushed ice: Cubed ice works too. Just stir a little longer.
history: The Mojito has Cuban roots and is tied to Havana, though its exact origin is disputed. Some trace it to a 16th-century medicinal drink, while others point to later Cuban bartending. It was popularized worldwide partly through Havana bars such as La Bodeguita del Medio.

seo.title: Mojito Recipe: White Rum, Mint, Lime and Soda
seo.description: Make a classic Mojito with 2 oz white rum, 1 oz lime juice, 2 tsp sugar, 8 mint leaves and soda water. Simple steps and pro tips.
